articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief Efforts
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Venezuela-related General License (GL) 60A, titled "Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela." This amended general license supersedes GL 60, dated June 25, 2026, and authorizes all transactions otherwise prohibited by the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations (VSR) that are related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela through April 21, 2027.

The authorization extends to the processing or transfer of funds on behalf of third-country persons to or from Venezuela in support of these authorized transactions. U.S. financial institutions and registered money transmitters can rely on the originator of a funds transfer for compliance, provided they do not know or have reason to know that the transfer is not in compliance.

However, GL 60A does not authorize the unblocking of any property blocked under the VSR, nor does it permit any other transactions or activities prohibited by other Executive Orders or parts of 31 CFR chapter V not specifically referenced in this general license. OFAC also issued one amended Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, in conjunction with this action.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Cuba Designation, and Issues New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations, a Cuba designation, and the issuance of new and amended general licenses and frequently asked questions. This action includes the designation of ABOLHASAN JALALI AND PARTNERS EXCHANGE COMPANY, an entity located in Qom, Iran, for its role in the Iranian financial network.

Additionally, OFAC is issuing Russia-related General License 128D, "Authorizing Certain Transactions Involving Lukoil Retail Service Stations Located Outside of Russia," and Russia-related General License 130B, "Authorizing Transactions Involving Certain Lukoil Entities in Bulgaria." An Iran-related General License FF, "Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance," has also been issued.

Furthermore, OFAC has issued a new Cuba-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 1276) and an amended Russia-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ 1225). The Cuban state-owned Banco Internacional de Comercio, S.A. (BICSA) has also been sanctioned.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan National Assembly President Jorge Jesus Rodriguez Gomez from SDN List
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has removed Jorge Jesus Rodriguez Gomez, the President of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. This designation removal, effective October 14, 2026, also included all four of his recorded aliases.

Rodriguez Gomez had been designated under Executive Order 13692 in September 2018. His removal follows that of his sister, Delcy Rodríguez, who was cleared on April 1, 2026. Both siblings now hold significant positions in Venezuela's interim government.

While this action restores Rodriguez Gomez's access to the U.S. financial system, he remains listed under Canada's Venezuela regulations, and reports indicate a separate U.S. visa restriction may still apply. He also continues to be considered a senior politically exposed person.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations. This action updates the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, targeting individuals and entities involved in illicit drug trafficking and global terrorism.

Among the additions to the SDN List are individuals and entities linked to the Cartel del Noreste's (CDN) criminal network, including its horse racing enterprise. These designations fall under the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations (31 C.F.R. part 594) and Executive Order 14059, which targets activities contributing to the international proliferation of illicit drugs.

This action underscores the Treasury's ongoing efforts to disrupt the financial networks of transnational criminal organizations and terrorist groups, aiming to prevent them from accessing the U.S. financial system.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, International Criminal Court Designations, and Burma-Related Removal
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, a freight forwarding firm, for apparent violations of sanctions regulations. Pegasus Worldwide Logistics has agreed to remit $175,015 to settle its potential civil liability for four apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and six apparent violations of the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations.

The violations occurred between September 2023 and February 2024, when Pegasus dealt in blocked property by facilitating the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company. Additionally, Pegasus failed to respond fully for six months to an OFAC subpoena.

In separate actions, OFAC also issued several International Criminal Court-related General Licenses (GLs 13, 14, 15, and 16) authorizing various transactions involving the International Criminal Court, including those related to telecommunications, enterprise software, pension payments, and certain detainees. Furthermore, OFAC announced a Burma-related designation removal.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Russia-Related General License Authorizing Diesel Fuel Transactions
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Russia-related General License (GL) 135, titled "Authorizing Transactions Related to the Sale, Delivery, Offloading, and Importation of Diesel Fuel of Russian Federation Origin." This general license temporarily authorizes certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited by the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions Regulations or the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The authorization is valid through April 7, 2027, and aims to address global energy market concerns amidst ongoing regional instability. This action follows a presidential announcement regarding a deal with Russia to release diesel fuel to global markets.

However, GL 135 explicitly states that it does not authorize debits to an account on the books of a U.S. financial institution of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, the National Wealth Fund of the Russian Federation, or the Ministry of Finance of the Russian Federation.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations and Amended Russia-Related General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations and the issuance of an Iran-related General License. This action is part of ongoing efforts to counter illicit financial activities linked to Iran.

In addition to the Iran-related actions, OFAC has also issued an amended Russia-related General License. This amendment, GL 13S, authorizes certain administrative transactions prohibited by Directive 4 under Executive Order 14024.

These actions reflect OFAC's continued focus on addressing threats from both the Iranian and Russian regimes through targeted sanctions and the strategic use of general licenses to manage the impact of sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Iran-Related Alert, Designations Removals, and Updates
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced several actions related to Iran, including designations removals, designations updates, and the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert. This alert aims to provide guidance and highlight risks associated with certain transactions involving Iran.

Alongside these updates, OFAC has also published an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question. These measures are part of a broader strategy to enhance the effectiveness of sanctions against Iran and to inform the public about potential evasion tactics.
The designations removals and updates reflect ongoing adjustments to the sanctions list based on new information and policy considerations, ensuring that the sanctions remain targeted and impactful.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Counter Terrorism Designations. These designations target individuals and entities involved in supporting terrorist activities globally, aiming to disrupt their financial networks and limit their ability to operate.

This action underscores OFAC's commitment to combating global terrorism by identifying and sanctioning those who provide material, financial, or technological support to terrorist organizations. The updated Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List reflects these new additions.
The designations are part of a continuous effort to protect the U.S. financial system from illicit finance and to prevent resources from reaching those who pose a threat to national security.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for $11.6 Million Over Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to remit $11,662,930 to settle its potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations of multiple OFAC sanctions programs. These programs include those targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism.

The apparent violations occurred when Bank of America processed correspondent banking payments through blocked banks due to technical and human error, allowed designated individuals to make payments and withdraw funds due to poor sanctions alert calibration, failed to promptly update watchlists following OFAC designations, and mishandled business accounts associated with blocked persons.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were non-egregious but largely not voluntarily self-disclosed. The settlement amount reflects no reduction to the base penalty, including no mitigation for remedial measures or cooperation.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Pays $175,015 to Settle OFAC Sanctions Violations
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, a freight forwarding firm, has agreed to remit $175,015 to settle its potential civil liability for four apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and six apparent violations of the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations.

The violations occurred between September 2023 and February 2024, when Pegasus dealt in blocked property by facilitating the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company. Additionally, the firm failed to respond fully for six months to an OFAC subpoena.

OFAC determined that Pegasus's conduct was non-egregious and not voluntarily disclosed. This settlement underscores the importance of due diligence and timely cooperation with OFAC inquiries for companies involved in cross-border shipments.

articles.headline: Individual Settles with OFAC for $1.4 Million in Sanctions Violations
body: An individual has settled with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for $1,427,230. The settlement addresses apparent violations of OFAC sanctions regulations. The specific details of the violations were not immediately released but typically involve transactions with sanctioned entities or jurisdictions.

OFAC civil penalties are assessed based on various factors, including the egregiousness of the violations, whether they were voluntarily self-disclosed, and the level of cooperation with OFAC's investigation. This significant penalty highlights OFAC's continued enforcement efforts against individuals who breach sanctions laws.

This action serves as a reminder to all U.S. persons, regardless of their professional capacity, of their obligations to comply with OFAC regulations to prevent illicit financial flows and protect national security interests.

articles.headline: Rice Lake Weighing Systems, Inc. Settles with OFAC for $60,764
body: Rice Lake Weighing Systems, Inc. has agreed to remit $60,764 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of sanctions regulations administered by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). The details of the apparent violations were not immediately specified.

OFAC's enforcement actions aim to ensure compliance with U.S. sanctions programs, which are critical for national security and foreign policy objectives. Companies are expected to implement robust compliance programs to prevent unauthorized transactions with sanctioned entities or jurisdictions.

This settlement underscores the importance for all U.S. companies, regardless of their size or industry, to conduct thorough due diligence and maintain effective sanctions compliance controls to avoid potential penalties.

articles.headline: FTI Consulting, Inc. Pays $1.05 Million to Settle OFAC Sanctions Violations
body: FTI Consulting, Inc. has agreed to remit $1,050,000 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of sanctions regulations administered by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). The specific nature of the violations was not detailed in the initial announcement.

This settlement highlights OFAC's continued focus on enforcing sanctions compliance across various industries, including professional services firms. Companies are expected to have comprehensive compliance programs in place to identify and mitigate sanctions risks.

The penalty serves as a reminder that even indirect involvement in transactions with sanctioned parties or jurisdictions can lead to significant financial consequences. OFAC encourages voluntary self-disclosure of apparent violations and cooperation with investigations.

articles.headline: Adani Enterprises Limited Settles with OFAC for $275 Million
body: Adani Enterprises Limited has agreed to remit $275,000,000 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of sanctions regulations administered by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This substantial penalty underscores the global reach of U.S. sanctions and the importance of compliance for international corporations.

While the specific details of the violations were not immediately disclosed, such large settlements typically involve significant and/or numerous transactions with sanctioned entities or jurisdictions. This action highlights the critical need for multinational companies to implement robust and effective sanctions compliance programs.

The settlement serves as a strong deterrent and a clear message from OFAC regarding its commitment to enforcing U.S. sanctions laws, even against major international players. Companies operating globally must ensure their operations do not inadvertently facilitate prohibited transactions.

articles.headline: TradeStation Securities, Inc. Pays Over $1.1 Million to Settle OFAC Violations
body: TradeStation Securities, Inc. has agreed to remit $1,110,661 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of sanctions regulations administered by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). The specific nature of the violations was not immediately detailed.

This enforcement action emphasizes the responsibility of financial institutions, including brokerage firms, to maintain stringent sanctions compliance programs. Such programs are essential to prevent transactions with individuals or entities on OFAC's various sanctions lists.

The settlement serves as a reminder that failures in screening, customer due diligence, or transaction monitoring can lead to significant penalties. OFAC continues to actively pursue enforcement against entities that do not adequately adhere to U.S. sanctions laws.

articles.headline: Individual Settles with OFAC for $3.7 Million Related to Syrian Sanctions Violations
body: An individual has settled with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for $3,777,000. This settlement addresses apparent violations of the Syrian Sanctions Regulations.

The significant penalty highlights OFAC's rigorous enforcement against individuals who engage in transactions prohibited by U.S. sanctions programs, particularly those related to designated countries like Syria. Such violations can involve a wide range of activities, including financial transactions, trade, or the provision of services.

This case underscores the importance for all U.S. persons to be aware of and comply with OFAC's sanctions regulations, as non-compliance can result in substantial financial penalties and other enforcement actions.

articles.headline: IMG Academy, LLC Settles with OFAC for $1.72 Million
body: IMG Academy, LLC has agreed to remit $1,720,000 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of sanctions regulations administered by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). The specific details of the apparent violations were not immediately released.

This settlement emphasizes the broad applicability of U.S. sanctions laws across various sectors, including educational and athletic institutions. Organizations are expected to implement robust compliance programs to prevent engagement in prohibited transactions with sanctioned individuals, entities, or jurisdictions.
The penalty serves as a reminder that all U.S. entities must conduct thorough due diligence and maintain effective sanctions compliance controls to avoid potential legal and financial repercussions.

articles.headline: US Inflation Rises to 3.7% in September, Fueling Rate Hike Concerns
body: United States consumer prices jumped in September, with annual inflation accelerating to 3.7 percent, up from 3.4 percent in August, according to the latest data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. This final inflation report before the pivotal midterm elections comes amid widespread dissatisfaction with the cost of living.

Gasoline prices accounted for over half of the overall monthly increase, surging 9.1% in September and up 34.2% over the past year. Fuel oil prices, used for heating, also shot higher, rising 15.3% in September and 74.2% annually. These higher energy costs are largely attributed to the ongoing war with Iran.

The uptick in consumer prices is putting pressure on the Federal Reserve to potentially raise interest rates for a second time this year. Economists are divided on whether the Fed will hike rates again or hold them steady, with market expectations pricing in a significant chance of a rate hike in December.
articles.source: Bureau of Labor Statistics / Al Jazeera / Reuters

articles.headline: OCC Imposes Record $750 Million Penalty on Bank of America for BSA/AML Failures
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has announced a record $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A., for widespread violations of the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and its implementing regulations. This marks the largest penalty in OCC history.

The OCC found that Bank of America's BSA/AML compliance program was deficient and ineffective, with its transaction monitoring system failing to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions. This led to the filing of a large number of late suspicious activity reports (SARs) involving billions of dollars, many of which indicated money laundering.

This enforcement action was taken in coordination with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), which assessed a $1.2 billion fine that credits the OCC's penalty, and OFAC, which announced an $11.6 million settlement. The OCC emphasized that banks of Bank of America's size and complexity must devote sufficient resources to detect and prevent money laundering.
articles.source: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency / U.S. Treasury

articles.headline: OCC Releases Report on Large Banks' 'Debanking' Practices, Considers Further Regulatory Changes
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has released a report detailing its supervisory review of large banks' 'debanking' activities, finding that all nine largest U.S. banks had policies between 2020 and September 2025 that restricted access to financial services for customers based on political or religious beliefs or lawful business activities.

The report, conducted in accordance with the President's Executive Order, “Guaranteeing Fair Access to Banking for All Americans,” identified public and nonpublic policies that limited access for certain industry sectors, including oil and gas, firearms, and digital asset activities. The OCC attributed much of the problem to "inexact" reputational risk policies.

Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan V. Gould stated that he is not confident current efforts by banks will be enough and that the OCC will assess further changes to the regulatory and supervisory framework to reduce the likelihood of these harmful practices recurring. The OCC, FDIC, and Federal Reserve have already taken steps to remove reputational risk from bank supervision.
articles.source: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OCC and Federal Reserve Issue Enforcement Actions Against American Express for AML Failures
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Federal Reserve have issued enforcement actions against American Express and its subsidiaries for significant deficiencies in their anti-money laundering (AML) programs. American Express National Bank received a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty from the OCC.

Regulators identified "enterprise-wide" AML program issues, particularly at the national bank subsidiary, which failed to adequately tailor its Bank Secrecy Act/AML risk assessment to its business activities. This resulted in systemic breakdowns in suspicious activity monitoring and reporting, leading to approximately $13 billion of suspected trade-based money laundering activity between June 2014 and May 2025.

The OCC emphasized that banks of American Express's size and complexity must dedicate sufficient resources to ensure compliance with AML laws and regulations, which are crucial for economic and national security. The bank is required to create an action plan within 90 days to address these deficiencies.
articles.source: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency / Banking Dive

articles.headline: Revisions to the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) revises the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China). This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
